Chapter 1 (Outline Holds the Line): W005 pink outline confirmed as primary readable contour. W097 white outline with splayed top confirmed. W213 yellow-outlined body with void face confirmed. Transitions are visually grounded.

W266 revised: the dominant mark is a central light bloom, not a clean band; transition language updated accordingly.

Chapter 3 (Crossed Marks and Competing Eyes): W052 red X marks confirmed. W084 asymmetric eye treatment confirmed. W278 vertical split confirmed. W274 two ringed circles as minimal face evidence confirmed. Transitions are visually grounded.

title: Heads Emerging from Darkness
question: Which marks let a face become visible against a dark ground?
introduction: Look for the marks that make a head distinguishable from dark surroundings. Contours, colored bands, crossed shapes and teeth offer different points of entry. Follow them across more layered or less clearly bounded surfaces. Compare what first draws your attention with the quieter shapes you locate after spending more time with the image.
closing: Return to a darker work and begin with a small accent. Which features become easier to find when you follow that mark?

chapters.title: Outline Holds the Face
chapters.introduction: Three works where a strong outer contour is the primary reason a face or figure stays readable against its dark surround — and where that contour begins to stretch or break.

stops.whyHere: A thick pink outline traces the central figure against deep brown-black; without it, the dense interior marks would dissolve into the ground.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #7

stops.whyHere: A loose white outline performs the same anchoring work, but here it frays upward into splayed lines, testing how far an outline can stretch before it stops containing.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both works use a single enclosing line against darkness, but where the pink contour in the first is firm and closed, this white outline opens and unravels at the top.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #110

stops.whyHere: The figure's yellow-outlined body is solid and readable; the face, replaced by a flat black rectangle, shows what happens when outline encloses nothing but more darkness.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The white outline above frays but still suggests a face; here the outline is intact yet the face it encloses is a void, reversing the problem entirely.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #225

chapters.title: Color Bands Cut Across
chapters.introduction: Four works where a horizontal bar or broad color zone slices through the face, becoming the single mark that most clearly locates a head within the dark field.

stops.whyHere: A single yellow-gold band cuts edge to edge across the eye zone; in a field of red-on-red, it is the one mark that unambiguously locates the face.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous outline defines a body but leaves the face dark; here a single horizontal stroke does the opposite, marking the face while the rest merges with its red ground.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #234

stops.whyHere: Yellow-gold sweeps bracket the figure above and below; the paired red cross-hatched circles read as eyes only because those bands frame the dark mass between them.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: In the previous work one band crosses the face; here bands sit above and below the figure, so the dark mass between them acquires a face-like reading by position alone.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #285

stops.whyHere: A broad green band and a yellow band slice through the skull mid-face, indifferent to the anatomy beneath, yet their crossing makes the skull's interior suddenly legible.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous bands frame a dark mass from outside; here the bands cut directly through a skull form, intersecting its structure rather than surrounding it.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #290

stops.whyHere: A blazing central bloom of light organizes the layered circular marks into a recognizable head; that glow functions as the band, the one element that holds the form together.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous bands are opaque and slice through; here the organizing mark is light itself, radiating outward from the center rather than imposed across it.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #93

chapters.title: Crossed Marks and Mismatched Eyes
chapters.introduction: Four works where X-marks, asymmetric eyes, or a split-face division are the visible device that gives each face its distinct character against the surrounding dark.

stops.whyHere: Two red X marks over the eye sockets are the sharpest contrast against the gold skull; they simultaneously locate the eyes and block them.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's central glow radiates outward from the eye zone; here red X marks occupy the same zone and close it off, swapping emission for cancellation.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #69

stops.whyHere: One eye carries a red X-crossed circle, the other a blue iris and dark pupil; the asymmetry between sealed and open makes the face feel off-balance in a way identical marks could not.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's two X marks treat both eyes identically; here the treatment splits—one eye crossed, one open—so the face holds two different states at once.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #252

stops.whyHere: A dark vertical line divides the face: warm amber-red on one side, cool blue-grey on the other; the split is the primary mark that makes the face visible as a face.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The asymmetry above is between two eye treatments; here the whole face is divided by a single vertical line, extending the split from one feature to the entire surface.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #283

stops.whyHere: The dark-green mass would be nearly formless without the two small ringed circles near the upper center; those circles are the only marks that propose a face inside the dense crossing lines.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous face is split but fully present; here a face is barely proposed—two ringed circles in a dense field are the only evidence a head is there at all.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #23

chapters.title: Enclosing Forms
chapters.introduction: Three works where the face sits inside a curved or hooded boundary, raising the question of how much of the face that enclosure actually brings forward versus conceals.

stops.whyHere: The rounded helmet-visor form encloses two asymmetric eyes and a gridded mouth; pale washes and a bright highlight suggest a reflective surface that shows a face without fully exposing it.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous face is barely legible inside dense marks; here a rounded enclosure with a bright highlight offers more structure, yet the face inside remains incomplete and asymmetric.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #104

stops.whyHere: A large face fills the frame but colored loops spill past the jaw into the black surround, so the enclosure the head should provide keeps leaking outward.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The helmet above holds its contents; here the face has no such shell, and its marks overflow into the surrounding dark, dissolving the boundary the helmet maintained.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #134

stops.whyHere: The yellow hood is the most solid enclosure in the gallery, yet the face inside it is the darkest void—red slashes and bared teeth are all that remain where a face should be.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous face leaks outward into darkness; here the enclosure is intact and opaque, but the darkness is now inside, behind the hood.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #38

chapters.title: When the Ground Wins
chapters.introduction: One works where the dark field or a competing surround overwhelms the face, leaving marks that suggest a head is present without fully delivering one — or abandoning the face altogether.

stops.whyHere: An amber ground, crossing blue bands, and scattered black masses offer no stable face; the looping lines and dots read as noise rather than features, the gallery's most dissolved image.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous hood contains darkness within a legible figure; here figure dissolves entirely—the amber field and black masses offer no face to locate.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #127
